newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Mondragon says casino closure order lifted.
newsitem.headline: Mondragon says casino closure order lifted.

text.p: Mondragon International Philippines Inc said on Friday a government closure order on its casino unit was lifted on Friday.

Mondragon International chairman Jose Antonio Gonzalez said after a meeting with senior government officials that a three-person arbitration panel will be formed to resolve the dipute with the state-run Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corp (Pagcor).
Pagcor had earlier said it had rescinded the authority of Mondragon Leisure and Resorts Corp (MLRC) to operate a casino inside the Clark freeport area.
Pagcor was not immediately available for comment but residents in the Clark Special Economic Zone, where the casino is located, said it was open.
Mondragon Leisure, a subsidiary of Mondragon International Philippines Inc, is the operator of a hotel inside the Clark zone.
Pagcor also operates a casino near the Clark zone.

Pagcor chairman Alice Reyes said that Mondragon had continuously violated some provisions of their agreement which states that the Mondragon casino shall cater only to "foreigners, Filipino U.S. greencard holders and walk-in Filipino customers/casino players".
"It (the order) had no basis in law because everybody is entitled to due process," Gonzalez said. "We have never closed. They attempted to close but we never closed."
In fact, Gonzalez said he had asked the Philippine Stock Exchange this morning to suspend the trading of Mondragon to protect investors because of the news that its casino licence had been revoked.
But the exchange did not think there was any basis for a suspension, Gonzalez said.

Reyes claimed Mondragon had come out with marketing strategies which actively enticed Filipinos to patronise the Mondragon casino by granting limousine services, reimbursement of incidental travel expenses, free use of its hotel rooms and discounts on losses of players.
Mondragon shares have fallen over the past few days on persistent rumours of a pending closure, but company officials had dismissed the possibility.
However, Mondragon shares closed 65 centavos higher at 10.25 pesos on Friday after the company announced positive results forecasts for 1996 and 1997.
